title: Industrial Automation & PLCs
subtitle: Relays, ladder logic and programmable logic controllers — how machines are controlled and kept safe.
outcomes: Explain how relays, contactors and time-delay relays switch machines
Read and draw ladder logic for control circuits
Design interlocks, motor controls and fail-safe circuits
Explain how PLCs, sensors and machine vision automate production

pool.q: What is a solenoid?
options: A coil that moves a magnetic object when energised with electric current
A computer that runs ladder logic
pool.explain: The coil's magnetic field can be switched on and off with the current.
pool.evidence: If we place a magnetic object near such a coil for the purpose of making that object move when we energize the coil with electric current, we have what is called a solenoid .

pool.q: What is the movable magnetic object in a solenoid or relay called?
pool.explain: Most armatures can be moved with DC or AC coil current.
pool.evidence: The movable magnetic object is called an armature , and most armatures can be moved with either direct current (DC) or alternating current (AC) energizing the coil.

pool.q: What happens to the magnetic field of a coil as the current through it increases?
pool.explain: Greater current means a stronger magnetic field, other factors being equal.
pool.evidence: The greater the current, the greater the strength of the magnetic field, all other factors being equal

pool.q: Which of these can solenoids be used for?
options: Opening door latches, opening or shutting valves and actuating switch mechanisms
pool.explain: A solenoid turns electric current into mechanical movement.
pool.evidence: Solenoids can be used to electrically open door latches, open or shut valves, move robotic limbs, and even actuate electric switch mechanisms.

pool.q: What can time-delay relays delay?
options: Armature motion on coil energisation, de-energisation, or both
The speed of light in the wires
pool.explain: That gives the relay time-delay actuation.
pool.evidence: Time-delay relays can be constructed to delay armature motion on coil energization, de-energization, or both.

pool.q: Besides normally-open or normally-closed, what else must be specified for a time-delay relay contact?
options: The number of rungs in the ladder
Whether the delay operates in the direction of closing or of opening
pool.explain: This gives the four basic types of time-delay contacts.
pool.evidence: Time-delay relay contacts must be specified not only as either normally-open or normally-closed, but whether the delay operates in the direction of closing or in the direction of opening.

pool.q: What is a protective relay for?
options: Monitoring electrical measurements to trigger a circuit breaker to open in an abnormal condition
Measuring how long a lamp is on
pool.explain: Protective relays monitor current, voltage, frequency and more.
pool.evidence: Protective relays A special type of relay is one which monitors the current, voltage, frequency, or any other type of electric power measurement either from a generating source or to a load for the purpose of triggering a circuit breaker to open in the event of an abnormal condition.

pool.q: How do protective relays monitor large AC currents?
options: Through current transformers (CTs) around the current-carrying conductors
By measuring the temperature of the room
Through wireless sensors on the roof
pool.explain: CTs step the current down to a 0 to 5 amp range.
pool.evidence: Protective relays can monitor large AC currents by means of current transformers (CT's), which encircle the current-carrying conductors exiting a large circuit breaker, transformer, generator, or other device.

pool.q: What are ladder diagrams used for?
pool.explain: They are specialised schematics for control logic.
pool.evidence: Ladder diagrams are specialized schematics commonly used to document industrial control logic systems.

pool.q: Why are ladder diagrams called "ladder" diagrams?
options: They were invented by a firefighter
They are always drawn on ladders
They show the career ladder of electricians
They have two vertical rails (supply power) and horizontal rungs for each control circuit
pool.explain: Rails supply power; each rung is a control circuit.
pool.evidence: They are called "ladder" diagrams because they resemble a ladder, with two vertical rails (supply power) and as many "rungs" (horizontal lines) as there are control circuits to represent.

pool.q: Where is the load device (lamp, relay coil, solenoid coil) usually drawn on a rung?
options: In the middle of the left rail
At the right-hand side of the rung
pool.explain: Which end of the supply is grounded matters for reliable operation.
pool.evidence: In ladder diagrams, the load device (lamp, relay coil, solenoid coil, etc.) is almost always drawn at the right-hand side of the rung.

pool.q: What do the L1 and L2 designations in a ladder diagram usually refer to?
options: The two poles of a 120 VAC supply
pool.explain: They are the two sides of the power supply, unless noted otherwise.
pool.evidence: The "L 1 " and "L 2 " designations refer to the two poles of a 120 VAC supply, unless otherwise noted.

pool.q: What is a permissive in a control system?
options: A process condition that must be met before equipment is allowed to start
pool.explain: Permissive switch contacts are wired in series.
pool.evidence: Each process condition is called a permissive , and each permissive switch contact is wired in series, so that if any one of them detects an unsafe condition, the circuit will be opened

pool.q: Why are permissive switch contacts wired in series?
options: So that all of them must fail before anything happens
So that if any one detects an unsafe condition, the circuit opens
pool.explain: Any single unsafe condition breaks the series string.
pool.evidence: If any one of the permissive conditions are not met, the series string of switch contacts will be broken, CR 2 will de-energize, and the red lamp will light.

pool.q: In a reversing motor circuit, what would happen if both contactors were energised at once?
options: The motor would run twice as fast
Phases A and B would be short-circuited together
pool.explain: That is why an interlock prevents one contactor while the other is on.
pool.evidence: If someone were to do that, phases A and B would be short-circuited together by virtue of the fact that contactor M 1 sends phases A and B straight to the motor and contactor M 2 reverses them

pool.q: What does the normally-closed "OL" contact in a motor control circuit protect against?
options: Thermal overload: if the heaters get too hot it opens and stops either contactor energising
pool.explain: OL is the thermal overload contact.
pool.evidence: If the heaters get too hot, the contact will change from its normal (closed) state to being open, which will prevent either contactor from energizing.

pool.q: Which type of failure is statistically most likely in electric circuits?
options: "Open" failures such as broken connections or blown fuses
Failures caused by too much voltage
pool.explain: So circuits should be designed to tolerate open failures.
pool.evidence: The nature of electric circuits is such that "open" failures (open switch contacts, broken wire connections, open relay coils, blown fuses, etc.) are statistically more likely to occur than any other type of failure.

pool.q: In fail-safe design, why is a false alarm better than a silent failure?
options: False alarms make the plant faster
Workers learn the alarm system failed and needs repair, instead of it failing when needed
pool.explain: Design the circuit so a wiring failure sounds the alarm.
pool.evidence: That way, a failure in the wiring would result in a false alarm, a scenario much more preferable than that of having a switch silently fail and not function when needed.

pool.q: What is the goal when engineering a circuit with open failures in mind?
options: Use as many fuses as possible
Make it as tolerant as possible to such a failure
pool.explain: Open failures are the most likely, so design for them.
pool.evidence: With that in mind, it makes sense to engineer a circuit to be as tolerant as possible to such a failure.

pool.q: What was the purpose of the PLC (programmable logic controller)?
options: To replace electromechanical relays with a solid-state computer running a stored program
pool.explain: A PLC emulates many interconnected relays.
pool.evidence: The purpose of a PLC was to directly replace electromechanical relays as logic elements, substituting instead a solid-state digital computer with a stored program, able to emulate the interconnection of many relays to perform certain logical tasks.

pool.q: What does a PLC read through its input terminals?
options: "High" and "low" logical states from sensors and switches
pool.explain: Outputs then power lights, solenoids and contactors.
pool.evidence: A PLC has many "input" terminals, through which it interprets "high" and "low" logical states from sensors and switches.

pool.q: Why was the PLC programming language designed to resemble ladder logic diagrams?
options: Because computers cannot use other languages
To make PLCs harder to copy
Because ladder diagrams are faster to run
So electricians used to ladder schematics would feel comfortable programming it
pool.explain: Familiar notation made PLCs easy to program.
pool.evidence: In an effort to make PLCs easy to program, their programming language was designed to resemble ladder logic diagrams.

pool.q: Which company released the MODICON in the late 1960s?
pool.explain: The device became known generically as a PLC.
pool.evidence: In the late 1960's an American company named Bedford Associates released a computing device they called the MODICON .

pool.q: What is computer-aided design (CAD)?
options: Using computers to design and test new products and modify existing ones
pool.explain: CAM uses computers to develop and control production.
pool.evidence: In computer-aided design (CAD), computers are used to design and test new products and modify existing ones.

pool.q: What does computer-aided manufacturing (CAM) do?
options: Uses computers to develop and control the production process
pool.explain: CAD/CAM links design, testing and manufacturing control.
pool.evidence: Computer-aided manufacturing (CAM) uses computers to develop and control the production process.

pool.q: What are robots, as defined in the lesson?
options: Computer-controlled machines that can perform tasks independently
pool.explain: Robotics is the technology of designing, building and operating them.
pool.evidence: Robotics Robots are computer-controlled machines that can perform tasks independently.

pool.q: Who used the first robot, the "steel-collar worker", and when?
pool.explain: Robots can be mobile or fixed in one place.
pool.evidence: The first robot, or “steel-collar worker,” was used by General Motors in 1961.

pool.q: How are IoT applications described in the lesson?
options: Things (devices) sending data that generates insights
pool.explain: IoT services give insights over the devices' data.
pool.evidence: IoT applications can be described as things (devices) sending data that generates insights .

pool.q: In the fruit quality prototype, what triggers the IoT application?
options: A manager pressing a button daily
pool.explain: A sensor detects the fruit and starts the quality check.
pool.evidence: You will learn how to architect a fruit quality control system prototype, including about using proximity sensors to trigger the IoT application, and what the architecture of this prototype would be.

pool.q: What is a reference architecture?
options: A building plan for a factory
The final version of a product
An example architecture to use as a reference when designing new systems
pool.explain: You can substitute your own devices and services.
pool.evidence: A reference architecture is an example architecture you can use as a reference when designing new systems.

pool.q: The three components of architecting an IoT application are
The component that communicates between the things and the components that create insights is:
How do time of flight proximity sensors work?
options: They send laser beams and time how long till they bounce off an object
They use sound and measure how long till the sound bounces off an object
